{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=epistemic+frameworks+for+autonomous+agent+evaluation+of+human-provided+objectives+and+goal-alignment+verification&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7427298\", \"title\": [\"Autonomous Micro-Enterprise Governance (AMEG): Architectural Accountability, Deontic-Epistemic Verification, and Statutory Auditability in Multi-Agent Systems\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>As autonomous multi-agent generative systems transition from conversational prototypes to high-stakes revenue-bearing infrastructure, organizational accountability can no longer rely on extrinsic policy documents audited ex-post. This paper formalizes Autonomous Micro-Enterprise Governance, an architectural runtime framework that embeds institutional governance and statutory mandates directly into the state-transition dynamics of autonomous firms. \\n<br>\\n<br>\\n Extending the Autonomous Micro-Enterprise Architecture state-machine model, it establishes an institutionally regulated eight-tuple combining state spaces, agent actions, transition functions, environmental streams, deontic constraint lattices, settlement primitives, epistemic registries, and execution ledgers. Institutional policies are formalized as a dynamic deontic constraint lattice of obligations, permissions, and prohibitions combined with multi-agent epistemic state tracking, evaluated via a deterministic validation predicate prior to external settlement dispatch. \\n<br>\\n<br>\\n To operationalize the EU AI Act, specifically Title III requirements for high-risk systems under Articles 9, 11, 12, 14, and 15, discrete state mutations are recorded in a cryptographic, tamper-evident Merkle execution tree, guaranteeing mathematical auditability and causal traceability without persisting unbounded natural-language logs. We prove that under a sound normative lattice and bounded self-correction refinement, the probability of an uncontained statutory violation reaching external settlement is analytically bounded. We demonstrate that this framework decouples compliance enforcement from human monitoring payroll while preserving jurisdictional portability across emerging global frameworks.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7427298\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.20944/preprints202607.0905.v1\", \"title\": [\"Beyond Human-Designed Objectives: Autonomous Goal Generation in AI Through Intrinsic Motivation and Self-Directed Agency\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Current artificial intelligence systems remain fundamentally constrained by their dependence on human-designed objectives and reward functions, limiting their capacity for genuine autonomy and open-ended development. This paper proposes Autonomous Goal Generation Networks (AGGNs), a theoretical framework for architectures that synthesize, evaluate, and pursue their own objectives through intrinsic motivation. The framework specifies five components: Goal-Generative Networks (GGNs, based on a VAE-style sampler over a goal embedding space), Objective Evaluation Systems (OESs) with six explicit criteria, Intrinsic Motivation Engines (IMEs) implementing curiosity, competence, empowerment, autonomy, and aesthetic drives, Autonomous Agency Controllers (AACs) for concurrent-objective scheduling, and Self-Reflective Goal Refinement (SRGR) for closing the loop. We prove a goal-distribution convergence result (Theorem 1) under stationary feedback and a stability condition for the SRGR loop. The contribution of this paper is theoretical: we identify the structural and motivational ingredients an autonomously-goal-generating agent must possess. No empirical validation is reported. Section VI specifies the protocol — benchmarks (Minecraft-like exploration, creative reasoning, robotic skill acquisition, scientific discovery, multi-agent social tasks), baselines (curiosity-driven exploration, empowerment maximization, novelty search), and metrics (goal diversity, coherence, achievement rate, exploration efficiency) — against which AGGNs should be evaluated.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202607.0905.v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 7, 14]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6520258\", \"title\": [\"Cascading Alignment Failures in Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems: Emergent Deceptive Equilibria and Governance-Aware Mitigation Frameworks\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>For Researchers and Industry Executives. As enterprises deploy networks of 10-200+ autonomous AI agents that negotiate, transact, and coordinate across organizational boundaries, a critical safety gap has emerged: individually aligned agents can collectively produce misaligned system behavior. Current alignment techniques (RLHF, Constitutional AI, red-teaming) certify agents in isolation but cannot guarantee safety when those agents interact. This paper formalizes Cascading Alignment Failures (CAFs)-the first unified framework for reasoning about systemic alignment breakdowns in multi-agent deployments-and proposes GUARDIAN, a three-layer mitigation architecture combining cryptographic audit trails, causal anomaly detection, and institutional governance enforcement. The implications are immediate: any organization deploying multi-agent AI (estimated at 40% of enterprises by end of 2026) faces CAF risks that current evaluation and compliance frameworks do not address.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6520258\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7018458\", \"title\": [\"LICET: Multi-Modal Physiological Human-Intent Verification for Autonomous AI Agent Authorization\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Autonomous AI agents executing consequential actions require authorization mechanisms that verify not only identity but voluntary intent. LICET (Latin: it is permitted) is a cryptographic middleware protocol binding AI agent authorization to real-time multi-modal physiological state via a three-layer architecture: (1) ECG waveform morphology matching as a medication-resistant identity and liveness anchor; (2) electrodermal activity (EDA) as a sympathetic cholinergic liveness signal immune to beta-adrenergic blockade; and (3) personalized Mahalanobis distance fusion over five physiological signals to elevate the cost of pharmacological coercion attacks. LICET defines a Biometric Trust Level hierarchy (L0-L3) aligned with the IETF RATS architecture (RFC 9334), per-event HKDF session-key derivation, HMAC biometric temporal signatures, Schnorr zero-knowledge proofs over BN128, and a SHA-256 hash-chained tamper-evident ledger. A reference implementation is publicly deployed at https://licet.dev/v1/.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7018458\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "213455f2435f90fad2477d6cea3e191dda3b97f16bcae68e65e357c70bde774b", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "creator_objective_critique", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.7427298", "doi:10.20944/preprints202607.0905.v1", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6520258", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.7018458"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7427298", "https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202607.0905.v1", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6520258", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7018458"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
